problem: The text names CoNLL shared tasks as a source of WSD test sets. The CoNLL shared tasks cover chunking, NER, dependency parsing, SRL and similar tasks; they did not run a word sense disambiguation task. Sense-tagged WSD evaluation data comes from the Senseval and SemEval campaigns.
fix: Standard test sets come from the Senseval and SemEval campaigns, in lexical sample and all-words form.

problem: Section 1 says the window k is 'usually between 5 and 50' words to each side, but Section 3 says supervised WSD uses a window of 'usually ±5 to ±10'. The two statements contradict each other and a student will not know which figure to quote.
fix: Give one range. In Section 1 write: the window is k words to each side, with k usually between 5 and 10 in supervised systems; the whole sentence can be used when data are scarce.

problem: The bare claim contradicts Section 3, which lists part-of-speech tags, collocations and dependency features as separate evidence. A student may read it as 'no other features exist'.
fix: Context is the main evidence, taken from the words, their part-of-speech tags and their syntactic relations around the target.

problem: 'a pronoun-free word three sentences later can still settle the sense' is unclear: 'pronoun-free word' has no defined meaning here, so the point about document-level evidence is lost.
fix: One sense per discourse means that another occurrence of the same word three sentences later can still correct the sense, so a document-level pass often helps.
